prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Editorial interior for a top design magazine: a Nordic girl's room, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.0 m, a child's eye height, level, straight verticals, all sharp. Hero: the bed nook in the window corner on the left third, the desk corner with its two prints on the right.

2. LIGHT. Only key: diffuse daylight from the north window on the left, no direct sun; no lamp is lit in this frame. Exposed for the walls: the white wall above the colour band beside the window reads clean warm white, just under the glowing reveal; the glass one step brighter and still detailed, a pale winter garden. Daylight falls across the bed covers from the left and fades a gentle half stop toward the desk. Each piece has a lit left face and a right side about one stop darker; bed and desk throw long feathered shadows to the right and toward the camera, short dense contact shadows. The ceiling a touch darker than the walls. White balance 4600 K: the wall above the band stays warm white, never pink, yellow or grey; real contrast, never milky.

3. MATERIALS. Upper walls matte mineral paint #F4F1EC; a crisp blush-clay band #E8D5CC to 1.25 m on the bed and desk walls, skirting in the same blush. Floor wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E. Bed and desk: oiled oak #C8A27A with a soft satin sheen, one long soft window highlight along the bed rail and desk top and down the planks; no mirror reflection.

4. PRODUCTS, exactly these:
a. ROMAN BLIND inside the window reveal, cut by the top and left edges: flat beige linen roman blind folded up to 1.85 m, no visible cord.
b. PRINTS above the desk: two 30 x 40 framed prints, charcoal flower silhouettes on cream, thin light frames, each about a third of the desk's length.
c. BOOKSHELF over the bed foot: two tiers of two natural light-wood face-out ledges with a front bar, each tier about half the bed's length; picture books face-out, covers in blush, oat and warm white, no readable text.
d. RUG between bed and desk, cut by the bottom edge: a 140 x 200 flat-woven jute and cream rug with soft overlapping shapes.
e. BEDDING: single duvet cover and pillowcase in warm cream crinkled cotton muslin.
f. On the foot third of the bed: a beige six-layer cotton muslin blanket, folded.
g. At the head, against the wall: two 40 cm corduroy windmill-patchwork cushions, milky white and dusty pink.
h. In front of them: a small cream crochet bunny, embroidered eyes, about a cushion's height.
i. On the rug, cut by the bottom edge: a jute rope cylinder basket with loop handles, three knitted balls in blush, oat and white in it.
j. DESK, left end: a 35 cm soft linen bunny doll in an oat cloth dress, sitting against the wall; the rest of the desk bare.

5. NOT IN FRAME: ceiling lamp, wall lamp, chair, doll pram, pen cup, other toys, clothes, books off the shelf, screens, plastic, socket, cable, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, glow halos, HDR look, grain or vignette.

grade.rule: docs/render-recipe-nordic-2026-10-24.md 2.6: WB on the hero-wall patch, exposure capped +-0.2 stop, chroma -10%, roll-off from L 94, S curve 0.12, black point to L 12.5 only if below 12, no grain, no vignette

clay_lock.method: regions = whole frame, quadrants, ceiling/floor bands and the clay boxes of fixed furniture / windows / openings; peaks below ~0.03 are unreliable (weak texture), so the verdict is visual (<aid>-lock.png) with the strong-peak number as support
